title: The Atlas is the human-readable constitutional anchor of a larger machine-readable Synome
content:
A.1.3.1.1 reframes the Atlas as a component rather than the whole: "The Atlas is part of a larger Synome. The Synome is the comprehensive machine-readable structure that contains the Atlas as its constitutional anchor node and additionally contains all other documents that operationalize the principles, rules, and processes specified by the Atlas. The Atlas is the human-readable, governance-voted entry point to the Synome."

A.1.3.1.2 fills in the rest: Synome Documents are machine-readable non-Atlas documents — "specifications expressed in a programming language, formula files, and similar machine-readable artifacts" — explicitly including those forming part of Agent Artifacts.

The architectural claim is a clean separation of two properties that usually get muddled in on-chain governance: **what is voted on** and **what executes**. Humans vote on human-readable text; machines execute machine-readable artifacts; the two are formally linked with the Atlas as the anchor node. This is what lets Sky govern software and AI agents without asking token holders to vote on code diffs, and without letting code be the de facto rule.

The phrase "constitutional anchor node" is doing real work. In a graph of dependencies, an anchor is where authority terminates — every Synome Document's legitimacy traces back through the graph to Atlas text. That is only meaningful because of the supremacy rule in A.1.3.1.4; without it, the anchor would be decorative.
description: A.1.3.1.1 makes the Atlas the governance-voted entry point; Synome Documents are the code, formulas and specifications that operationalize it, including Agent Artifacts.
